t: You're looking at the King Edward Building, which for most of the twentieth century was London's main Post Office. It was also the main sorting office for the EC postal area and for overseas mail. It opened in 1910 and closed in the 1990s. The architect was Sir Henry Tanner, who worked for HM Office of Works and was a prominent British architect of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. So this is a government-built piece of postal infrastructure, designed by one of the state's own architects.
